scenarios.name: Fed Pivot to Rate Cuts
scenarios.description: Inflation continues to moderate toward 2.5-3% range, prompting Fed to begin cutting rates in Q4 2026 with 75-100bps of cuts by mid-2027. Financial conditions ease, supporting interest-sensitive sectors.

impacts.explanation: Fed cuts rates as inflation moderates, reducing policy rate from 3.63% to ~2.9%
Lower policy rate expectations and reduced term premium pull long-term yields down
Easier financial conditions boost investment and consumption, adding ~0.8pp to growth
Stronger growth reduces slack, modestly lowering unemployment from 4.1%
Lower mortgage rates revive housing demand, reversing recent decline
Improved consumer confidence and lower borrowing costs support spending
Inflation continues gradual moderation toward target, consistent with Fed reaction function

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Fed cutting cycles historically begin 6-12 months after last hike when inflation trends down. Current inflation at 3.35% YoY (per data) shows deceleration from peaks. Inside view: labor market softening (payrolls +0.1%) and flat industrial production suggest restrictive policy is biting. Clashing forces: sticky services inflation vs. goods deflation. Probability reflects 60% chance inflation cooperates * 45% chance Fed acts preemptively = ~27%, rounded to 28%.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems
Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence

scenarios.name: Inflation Re-acceleration & Fed Hold
scenarios.description: Services inflation proves sticky, energy prices surge on geopolitical supply disruption, and fiscal deficits maintain demand pressure. Fed holds rates at 3.63% through H1 2027, with hiking bias returning.

impacts.explanation: Fed maintains restrictive stance, keeping rates at 3.63%
Higher inflation expectations and term premium push 10Y toward 5.4%
CPI YoY rises from 3.35% to ~4.5% on energy and services persistence
Higher real rates and uncertainty dampen investment and consumption
Growth slowdown increases slack, pushing unemployment to ~4.4%
Higher borrowing costs and weaker global demand reduce manufacturing output
Mortgage rates near 7%+ continue to suppress construction activity

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: ~30% of disinflation episodes see significant re-acceleration (1970s, 2021-22). Inside view: Federal debt at $39T (+1.43%) implies persistent fiscal stimulus; trade deficit widening (+24.44%) suggests strong import demand. Clashing forces: wage growth moderation vs. shelter inflation stickiness. Probability: 40% chance inflation sticks * 55% chance Fed prioritizes credibility = 22%.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem
Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

scenarios.name: Geopolitical Supply Shock (Middle East/Energy)
scenarios.description: Escalation of Middle East conflict disrupts oil supply through Strait of Hormuz, pushing Brent crude to $110-120/bbl. Global trade routes disrupted, sanctions enforcement tightens.

impacts.explanation: Energy price spike feeds through to headline CPI and core via transportation/input costs
Terms-of-trade shock reduces real income; uncertainty freezes capex
Inflation expectations spike; flight-to-safety partially offsets via lower real rates
Higher energy import bill widens goods deficit significantly
Energy-intensive manufacturing curtails output; supply chain disruptions
Gasoline price surge crowds out discretionary spending
Fed hikes 25bps to anchor expectations despite growth hit

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Major Middle East oil supply disruptions ~15% per decade (1973, 1979, 1990, 2019). Inside view: Current regional tensions elevated but spare capacity exists (OPEC+ cuts). Clashing forces: US strategic petroleum reserve depletion vs. non-OPEC supply growth. Probability reflects 35% escalation risk * 40% significant supply loss = 14%, rounded to 15%.
tetlockCommandments: Triage - Focus on questions where careful thinking pays off
Look for the errors behind your errors

scenarios.name: AI-Driven Productivity Boom
scenarios.description: Generative AI adoption accelerates across services sectors, delivering measurable productivity gains of 1.5-2% annually. Investment in data centers and semiconductors surges, boosting potential growth.

impacts.explanation: Productivity surge lifts potential growth; capex boom adds to demand
Strong labor demand in tech and AI-adjacent sectors; net job creation despite automation
Semiconductor and equipment manufacturing ramps up significantly
Productivity gains reduce unit labor costs, easing services inflation
Higher potential growth raises neutral rate (r*) and term premium
Real wage growth from productivity supports consumption
Higher nominal GDP growth improves debt-to-GDP trajectory modestly

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: General purpose technology booms (electricity, ICT) deliver 0.5-1.5pp productivity lift after 10-15 year lag. AI adoption curve faster. Inside view: Capex intentions surveys at record highs; Nvidia revenue doubling. Clashing forces: Measurement challenges (free digital services) vs. tangible output. Probability: 50% AI delivers as hoped * 35% macro-visible within 12 months = 17.5%, rounded to 18%.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems
Strike the right balance between under- and overconfidence

scenarios.name: Fiscal Consolidation & Debt Ceiling Crisis
scenarios.description: Debt ceiling standoff in early 2027 leads to government shutdown risk and eventual spending caps agreement. Fiscal impulse turns negative as deficit reduction measures bite.

impacts.explanation: Government spending cuts and uncertainty reduce aggregate demand
Deficit reduction slows debt accumulation rate from 1.43% to ~0.9% annualized
Public sector and contractor layoffs; confidence effects on private hiring
Lower deficit expectations reduce term premium; flight-to-quality during crisis
Government worker furloughs and contractor payment delays reduce spending
Demand reduction eases price pressures modestly
Weaker domestic demand reduces import intensity

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Debt ceiling crises occurred in 2011, 2013, 2023 - ~25% chance per Congress. Inside view: Divided government likely post-2026 midterms; debt at 122% GDP creates pressure. Clashing forces: Political brinkmanship vs. market discipline forcing compromise. Probability: 40% divided government * 25% crisis severity = 10%.

scenarios.name: China Hard Landing & Global Trade Fragmentation
scenarios.description: China's property crisis deepens, growth falls to 3.5%, triggering financial stress. Global supply chains fracture further as US/EU impose new tariffs on Chinese EVs, solar, semiconductors. Friend-shoring accelerates.

impacts.explanation: US exports to China plummet; supply chain reconfiguration costs raise import prices
Integrated supply chains disrupted; intermediate goods shortages
Tariffs and reshoring costs pass through to consumer and producer prices
Export drag and supply chain costs offset domestic demand resilience
Global risk-off drives flight to US Treasuries; lower global growth expectations
Manufacturing and export-oriented sectors shed jobs
Fed cuts to offset external shock, providing insurance against financial spillovers

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Emerging market hard landings ~5% per decade. China-specific: property sector 25% of GDP, unprecedented leverage. Inside view: Policy stimulus failing to revive confidence; youth unemployment hidden. Clashing forces: Chinese stimulus capacity vs. structural headwinds. Probability: 20% hard landing * 35% significant US spillover = 7%.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem
Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

weightedForecasts.equation: 39065421 * (1 + 0.012) = 39532000 (weighted average of scenario debt growth rates)

methodology: Applied Tetlock's superforecasting framework: (1) Established base rates for each scenario using historical frequencies (outside view). (2) Decomposed each scenario into causal sub-mechanisms (granular analysis). (3) Identified clashing forces (e.g., inflation persistence vs. disinflationary productivity). (4) Assigned precise probabilities reflecting degrees of doubt. (5) Weighted scenario impacts by probability to generate forecasts. (6) Calibrated confidence intervals based on scenario dispersion and historical forecast errors. (7) Documented reasoning for auditability and future error analysis.
geopoliticalSummary: Elevated tensions in Middle East (Israel-Iran proxy conflict, Red Sea shipping risks), Russia-Ukraine war entering third year with no resolution, China-Taiwan strait tensions managed but fragile. US alliance cohesion strong (NATO expansion, AUKUS, Quad) but Global South non-alignment growing. Sanctions regimes expanding (Russia, Iran, China tech). Geopolitical risk premium embedded in energy and defense spending.
geoeconomicSummary: Global trade fragmenting into blocs (friend-shoring, near-shoring). US-China trade at record lows as % of GDP. Supply chains diversifying but not fully resilient. Dollar dominant but facing gradual erosion in settlement (BRICS expansion, bilateral currency agreements). Commodity markets tight with underinvestment in traditional energy and critical minerals. Industrial policy subsidies proliferating (IRA, CHIPS, EU Green Deal).
currentEventsSummary: Fed in restrictive hold after 2024-25 hiking cycle; inflation above target but trending down. Labor market cooling gradually (payrolls +0.1%, unemployment 4.1%). Fiscal deficit ~6-7% GDP with debt at 122% GDP. Housing frozen by rate lock-in effect. AI capex boom underway. Consumer resilient but savings depleted. Election year policy uncertainty. Commercial real estate stress concentrated in office.
